rationale: The PLP likely failed due to a consent overlay (OneTrust) blocking rendering/scroll and dynamic loading that requires user interaction/scroll. Adding explicit consent handling, a short scroll routine, and resilient product selectors should allow items to materialize. URL normalization to /en-de/ prevents region traps and unintended redirects. The selector set uses common Moncler attributes and generic product-card fallbacks without disrupting existing keys.
code_hints: Use a realistic desktop UA and enable stealth/anti-detection options. Keep headful if bot friction persists.
On navigation, immediately try clicking OneTrust consent (#onetrust-accept-btn-handler). Retry after a short wait if first attempt fails.
After consent, wait for one of the PLP item selectors. If not found, perform incremental scrolling (6 steps, 800ms pauses) and re-check.
Guard against overlay blocking: if a visible modal or backdrop exists ([class*='consent'], [class*='modal'], .ot-sdk-row), attempt to close it before querying tiles.
Treat PLP items as anchors linking to /p/ on moncler.com. Extract href, then navigate to PDP and read PDP price/title via the provided selectors.
Use timeout budgeting: 12–15s total for PLP materialization (including scrolls). If still empty, reload once and repeat consent + wait.
Set Accept-Language to en-DE to reduce locale switches; verify final URL contains /en-de/ before extraction and rewrite if needed using url_rules.
